label: FASHION
title: Runway Dresses Made From Pickleballs, Socks and Grandma's Tablecloth
image_files: File:A pickleball paddle with two pickleballs.jpg
paragraphs: This runway dress is decorated with flowers made from cracked pickleballs.
Designer Joan Cabarrus, a nurse from Round Rock, Texas, collects broken balls from local courts, because pickleballs can't be recycled.
She softens them in a panini press for about forty-five seconds, then shapes them into neon pink and yellow flowers. Her purse is two pickleball paddles.
She is one of about forty designers in Austin Creative Reuse's Reuse on the Runway show. Others used antivenom vial tops and beads rolled from magazines.
In Sedona, Arizona, Jesselynn Desmond was named Sustainable Designer of the Year. She turned her grandmother's tablecloth, her only heirloom from her, into a couture-style look.
Her second look was a skirt made from thirteen men's diabetic socks. Her prize: one thousand dollars and four thousand in design credits. Which would you wear?
